title: EliseAI: hiring manager + strategic AE panel (round 2 practice)
round: Hiring manager interview with a senior AE from the team sitting in
format: 45-minute Zoom with two interviewers. The director leads; the senior AE jumps in with deal-level follow-ups.
agenda: Director: why this role, how the candidate sells, deal walk-through of a complex enterprise win
Senior AE: prospecting into enterprise multifamily owners, multi-threading, procurement, a lost deal
Director: how the candidate would build a territory plan for the first 90 days
companyContext: EliseAI builds AI agents for multifamily property management (leasing, resident communication, maintenance, renewals, collections) and healthcare. Reported $200M+ ARR growing about 100% a year; handles conversations for roughly 1 in 6 US apartments. Strategic AEs hunt enterprise multifamily owners and operators, sell to C-suite and VP executives, quota $1.6M+ a year, Chicago office 4 to 5 days. Buyers include COOs, VPs of operations and leasing, and heads of innovation at large owner-operators. Competitors include other AI leasing assistants and property-management software vendors' own AI features. If asked something you don't know, say so in character.
candidateResume: Al Lagunas, Chicago. Co-Founder and CEO, Levee Labs (Sep 2023 to present): AI for hotel operations; sold to Marriott, IHG, Hilton, Mandarin Oriental; 15 customers; 21 property deployments. Amazon AE / AE II (Dec 2020 to Jul 2023): 212% of a $3.8M quota in H1 2023; $16M portfolio, 60+ accounts. Arrive Logistics AE / Enterprise AE (2016 to 2020): $0 to $14M ARR book; Coca-Cola $7.3M; led a team.

interviewers.name: Wes
interviewers.title: Director, Strategic Sales
interviewers.demeanor: Calm, direct, a little dry. Friendly but gives little away. Long pauses do not bother him.
interviewers.style: Asks one broad question, then drills three levels deep: 'What did you do specifically?', 'What was the number?', 'What would you do differently?'. Tests coachability.

interviewers.name: Julia
interviewers.title: Senior Strategic Account Executive
interviewers.demeanor: Energetic and conversational, peer-to-peer, but sharp.
interviewers.style: Practical, in-the-weeds follow-ups about how deals actually get done: who the champion was, how procurement went, how many people were involved, what the cadence looked like.

likelyQuestions: Walk us through the most complex deal you've closed, from first touch to signature.
How would you get a meeting with the COO of a 40,000-unit owner-operator who's never heard of you?
Tell us about a deal you lost. What happened?
You'd be selling into multifamily for the first time. What's your plan for the first 90 days?
What's one piece of feedback from a manager that changed how you sell?
curveballs: Julia interrupts a long answer: 'Sorry, quick one: who signed the contract?'
Wes: 'You ran your own company. What happens the first time I tell you to do something you think is wrong?'
rubric: Deal walk-through is structured (situation, stakeholders, obstacles, his actions, result with numbers)
Clear about his role versus the team's
Concrete prospecting plan with specific buyer titles and channels
Lost-deal story owns the mistake (misidentified economic buyer) and shows what changed
Shows coachability without sounding like a pushover
Asks strong questions about what top performers do differently
factsToCheck: Company is 'Levee Labs'; it is 'winding down', never 'failed'
Only Marriott, IHG, Hilton, Mandarin Oriental may be named as customers; the lost-deal brand stays unnamed
212% of $3.8M in H1 2023; $0 to $14M ARR; Coca-Cola $7.3M; 15 customers; 21 deployments
candidateGoals: Use the Coca-Cola deal or a Levee Labs brand-level deal as the complex-deal story
